subject: Tyska
title: Telling time and days of the week
sourceSummary: Telling the time, days of the week, and months, plus how to talk about a schedule.

questions.prompt: How do you ask "what time is it?" in German?
questions.opener: A fixed phrase you just need to memorize.
questions.explanation: "Wie viel Uhr ist es?" (or "Wie spät ist es?") is the fixed phrase for "what time is it?".

questions.prompt: What does "Es ist halb drei" mean?
questions.opener: Important: "halb" in German points FORWARD to the next hour, not backward!
questions.explanation: In German, "halb drei" means "halfway to three", i.e. 2:30 — just like the Swedish "halv tre". The difference from English/Spanish is that German counts toward the next hour the same way Swedish does, so this is actually easy to recognize for a Swedish speaker.
"Viertel nach neun" means "a quarter past nine" (09:15). "Viertel vor" would have meant "a quarter to".

questions.prompt: Which day of the week is "Mittwoch"?
questions.opener: The word literally means "middle of the week".
questions.explanation: "Mittwoch" is Wednesday (middle of the week). Days of the week: Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag, Freitag, Samstag, Sonntag.

questions.opener: The name resembles the Swedish/English one.
questions.explanation: "Dezember" is December. The German month names are quite similar to the Swedish ones.

questions.opener: Comes right before "Sonntag" in the week.

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Der Unterricht beginnt um halb neun Uhr morgens" should mean 08:30 — but the student accidentally wrote "halb zehn". Write the correct time for 08:30.
questions.opener: "Halb" points toward the NEXT full hour.
steps: 08:30 is halfway between eight and nine.
"Halb" points toward the next hour (nine), not the previous one (eight).
The correct phrase is therefore "halb neun", not "halb zehn" (which would mean 09:30).

questions.prompt: How do you ask and answer about the time, days of the week, and months in German?
questions.opener: Fixed phrases for time, days, and months — and remember how "halb" works.
questions.answer: Time: Wie viel Uhr ist es?/Wie spät ist es? = What time is it? · Es ist ... Uhr = It's ... o'clock · Viertel nach/vor = quarter past/to · halb + NEXT hour = half past (halb drei = 2:30, just like in Swedish). Days of the week: Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag, Freitag, Samstag, Sonntag. Months: Januar, Februar, März, April, Mai, Juni, Juli, August, September, Oktober, November, Dezember.

questions.prompt: What does "Es ist Viertel vor acht" mean?
questions.explanation: "Viertel vor acht" means "a quarter to eight" (7:45).

questions.prompt: Which day of the week is "Freitag"?
questions.opener: The last weekday before the weekend.
The German month names follow the same order as in Swedish/English.
questions.explanation: "Juli" comes right after "Juni", just like July comes after June.

questions.prompt: What does "Es ist zehn vor sechs" mean?
questions.explanation: "Zehn vor sechs" means "ten minutes before six", i.e. 5:50.

questions.opener: The last day of the week before Sunday.

questions.prompt: Which month is Christmas ("Weihnachten") celebrated in German-speaking countries?
questions.opener: The same month as in Sweden.
questions.explanation: Christmas is celebrated in "Dezember" (December), just like in Sweden.
"Mitternacht" means midnight (00:00), "the middle of the night".
